130.title: Elbow flexion during a down-the-line downswing

message_box.general: The general-purpose model underestimates the elbow bend, predicting a straighter arm than the reference pose.
message_box.specialized: The golf-specific model better captures elbow flexion and arm alignment.

99.title: Separating the arms at the face-on transition

message_box.general: The general-purpose model merges the left and right arm predictions in this pose.
message_box.specialized: The golf-specific model distinguishes both arms and preserves their separate joint connections.

29.title: Left–right shoulder assignment during the face-on transition

message_box.general: The general-purpose model swaps the left and right shoulders as the torso rotates.
message_box.specialized: The golf-specific model maintains the correct shoulder assignments and arm connections.

25.title: Arm estimation under motion blur in a face-on downswing

message_box.general: The general-purpose model misplaces the arm joints under motion blur.
message_box.specialized: The golf-specific model distinguishes the left and right arms despite blur and closely spaced hands.

101.title: Lead-arm occlusion during a down-the-line follow-through

message_box.general: The general-purpose model misplaces the lead wrist and elbow as the arm passes behind the torso.
message_box.specialized: The golf-specific model locates the lead-arm joints more accurately despite occlusion.

145.title: Severe arm occlusion during a down-the-line follow-through

message_box.general: The general-purpose model produces inconsistent joint locations when the arms are largely hidden by the torso.
message_box.specialized: The golf-specific model produces a more anatomically plausible pose, although some joint locations remain imperfect.
